summary:
A red-brick high-street shop house with a steep dark-slate front gable, built over one butcher's unit (a Folio and its door stalls) under a 9-wide maroon fascia, a red-and-white awning and two dark-oak pilasters. There is a separate lobby bay for the home stair, and two storeys of white-trimmed home windows mirrored about the gable. A lower two-storey back wing on the west makes the L, and the fenced vegetable garden behind (four beds, paths, gate from a side passage) reads as a family's plot. Red-brick high-street shop house, steep dark-slate front gable, L-plan with back wing and fenced kitchen garden; butcher's maroon fascia, striped awning and pink/brown/red display over one Folio plus stalls.
Shop at ground (sockets untouched), home on two floors above, loft; six trade parts. elements.md and plan.md sections written.

Masonry shell: Shell built: brick walls with deepslate plinth for main body and wing, quartz lintels, quoins, string courses and eaves bands, floors at y13/18/23 with stair wells and loft hatch, interior partitions and aisle partitions. Openings are left as air. make.sh produces a whole build.nbt, with no refused writes.
polish: Window sills (quartz slabs) and shutters are for the glazing part
Interior door leaves and glass are for the joinery part
elements.md items not ticked by me

Floor joists and stair wells at y13/18/23 with exact trimmer cuts

Walk reaches 14/14 rooms. The front render shows the windows, shutters and door correctly.

summary:
Roofs: Roofs part built: the main shop roof comes from roof.json (dark slate mix, dark oak verges, 2 dormers, chimney E kept, king-post trusses 5 at 2.83 m, worst member 0.85).
The back return's cottage roof (x 4..11, z 23..30, eave y 19, chimney S kept) is laid by parts/roof.mjs build(g) with the library's roof(), since runParts takes one roof spec.
./make.sh produces a whole build.nbt; the roof dry-run has no warnings. Four wing corner writes are refused by the shell's quoins.
polish: make.sh reports 4 REFUSED writes for the wing roof at (4,19,29), (4,19,30), (11,19,29), (11,19,30): the shell's smooth_quartz quoins sit at the wing's south eave corners, so the roof does not place stairs there. The corners are clean quartz, not a defect in the roof, but the part's line should show no refusals; the fix belongs to the shell (or the eave course moves).

The wing (cottage) roof has no trusses: roof.json is the only place trusses are declared and runParts takes one spec. The wing has no loft, so the frame is not needed for the look, but the simulation was not run on it.

The king-post trusses under the main roof show as 8 ORPHAN blocks in `mcd check` (stripped_dark_oak_log at 14..16, y 26..28, z 11 and 16; they hang from the ridge or stand off the rafters). They are structural members, not errors, but the check flags them.
Chimney E's stack goes through the main roof keep only; the render was checked from the street and back, not at the chimney close-up.

waste.what: Checked the roof by rendering and reading the tiles one at a time, and worked out the wing's overhang and keep coordinates by hand
waste.cost: 3 render/build cycles, about 4 minutes
waste.tool: A `mcd roof --dry-run` that reports refused cells per roof rect (and the eave course detected for each wall) before any build, so overhang/keep choices can be checked without a full make.sh

waste.what: Laid the second (wing) roof by calling the library's roof() directly inside a part, because runParts accepts only one roof spec
waste.cost: 1 extra file-writing step and one overhang edit after a REFUSED report (20 writes into the main rear wall)
waste.tool: runParts `roof` accepting an array of specs (or a roof.json with `secondary` rects), so each roof gets its own preset, eave y and keep

companions.task: Set the shell's wing corner quoins (x 4 and x 11, y 19, z 29..30) so the cottage roof's south eave corners can sit on them without a refused write, or give the eave course one more row.

summary:
Shopfront: Shopfront built in parts/shopfront.mjs: pilasters x9/x19, a 9x4 red_nether_bricks name board with BUTCHER in white/black banner letters, a one-row red/white awning with valance, cornice y13, hanging sign on an arm at x20, and the lobby hood at y9.
sockets.json display set (A1 pink_terracotta; A2 pink_terracotta, brown_mushroom_block, red_terracotta); wood stays dark_oak.
make.sh whole, Shopfront line shows 104 placed with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE; sockets check OK 0 problems; plan.md checklist and Notes updated.
polish: The awning is a single row (y 9) with its valance at z 3, so it reads thin from the street; a deeper awning or banner row would carry the colour better.
No shop lanterns under the awning or on the sign bracket (the keep-clear rules out z 4..5 at y 6..8; a bracket light needs its own design). The lobby hood's two lanterns are placed by the helper.
No window boxes or product-block panel on the piers: the product shows through the sockets.json display only.
elements.md has no tick column, so element items 2-6 are built but not ticked there. Item 7 is only half done: the hood is mine, and doorPair belongs to the joinery part.
The BUTCHER letters are banners (white cloth, black letters) placed by the part, not plaque, because plaque's dye pick gave off-palette banners; this is noted in plan.md Notes.

waste.cost: one full make and render cycle, about 2 retries
waste.tool: plaque/fascia need a base-colour option (base: 'white', letter: 'black') that keeps banners on palette, or fascia() should forward opts to plaque

waste.what: Checked the shopfront by eye from zoomed renders, with no pixel or colour check for whether each shop reads from the street.
waste.cost: 2 render passes
waste.tool: a mcd zoom/glance check that reports whether the fascia name and awning colour are legible from the street

waste.what: setDisplay rewrites sockets.json on every make, so the part has a file side effect during build.
waste.cost: 0 extra, but the file is touched on every run
waste.tool: sockets install --display / a display key in the layout, read by the build instead of written by it

waste.what: Worked out the fascia, pilaster and sign coordinates by hand from plan.md's tables instead of reading them from one structure.
waste.cost: about 10 coordinate checks
waste.tool: a plan-to-code table in plan.md or a plan.json read by the parts (plan.json exists but no helper reads it)

companions.task: Lay out BUTCHER in banner letters on the fascia (spacing, letter colour, legibility from the pavement), so the name reads at a glance.
Build the striped awning with a proper depth (more than one row) and a valance, and fix its brackets to the wall.
Hang lanterns under the awning and on the sign bracket, so the shop front is lit at night.

summary:
Chimneys, hearths and lights: Chimneys, hearths and lights built in parts/hearth.mjs: chimney E (x20..21 z13..14) and chimney S (x7..8 z31..32) with lit signal campfires, the living-room firebox at x18 z13..14, a wing range (lit furnace and smoker) at z29, and lanterns on iron_chain at y9 in the keeper's aisle and the lobby lane.
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt. The part's run shows 246 placed, 2 refused writes (earlier-part spruce_slab at 21,21,13 and 21,21,14), and no off-palette blocks.
Plan.md checklist ticked for hearth; elements.md items 12, 13, 14 ticked and 24 partly ticked; a Notes line records the refused cells and the living-room dark cell.
polish: Chimney E has a 2-cell gap at x21 y21 z13..14: an earlier part's spruce_slab sits where the stack's bricks should be. The roof or joinery owner should clear it; my part cannot write there.
The wing range at z29 has no flue through the south wall (z30) to chimney S. The shell has no opening there, so the smoke route is not built.
Living room (room-5) has one dark cell (min light 0) at the hearth end; room-5 should place its own light there.

Lobby stair hall and keeper's aisle floors read 8+ on the light map, except the lobby's stair-well end, which is the lane's own limit. Other rooms are still stubs, so their light is not measured here.
The signal_fire state is written by a second set() after chimneyStack, because the helper does not set it. This works, but it is a workaround.

waste.what: Worked out which earlier part owned the 2 refused cells at x21 y21 z13..14 by writing a one-off node script that loads build.nbt and reads blockAt cell by cell.
waste.cost: about 3 tool calls and 1 script run, plus a grep over the parts
waste.tool: parts-report.json should list the owning part and block for each refused cell (for example 'spruce_slab placed by Roofs at 21,21,13'), or runParts should print it.

waste.what: Tried lantern heights by rebuilding and re-running the light map three times: at y12 the aisle floor read 6-7, and at y9 on a chain it reads 9-C.
waste.cost: 3 make.sh runs and 3 light-map runs
waste.tool: mcd room / mcd light should suggest the lantern height and chain length that clears the dark cells in one pass, not only the spots at the ceiling.

waste.what: Set the signal_fire and lit states on the chimney campfires with a second g.set() after chimneyStack, because the helper leaves signal_fire out.
waste.cost: 2 extra writes and a re-check that the state stuck
waste.tool: vocab/h2.mjs chimneyStack should take { signal: true } and write signal_fire: "true" itself.

waste.what: Looked at the chimneys by eye from zoom tiles (zoom-chimE.png, zoom-chimS.png), with no automated check that a stack rises at least 2 blocks above the roof surface it passes through.
waste.cost: 2 zoom renders and 2 image reads
waste.tool: mcd check could report the stack's height above the roof surface it passes through.

waste.what: Placed the wing range furnace and smoker one by one, plus the brick hob above them, with no flue cell.
waste.cost: 4 set() calls
waste.tool: vocab/h3.mjs has no range helper; a hearth-style 'range' helper that also carves a flue through a named wall (with its opening recorded in plan.md) would cover the wing kitchen.

companions.task: Clear the spruce_slab sitting in chimney E's course at y21 (x21 z13..14) and confirm the stack passes through the eave cleanly, so the bricks run unbroken from the footing to the cap.
Cut the flue through the wing's south wall at x7..8 z30 and run it from the range at z29 up into chimney S, so the wing kitchen's smoke has a route out.
Light the living room's one dark cell at the hearth end (min light 0) with a chained lantern, so room-5 is lit to 8+ without relying on the firebox.

summary:
Grounds and garden: Grounds and garden built in parts/garden.mjs: passage (dirt with gravel edges), paths a/b/c with coarse-dirt edges, four farmland beds with spruce-slab rings and water, perimeter spruce fence with double gate at x22..23 z22, lamp post 25,21, fruit tree 23,35, podzol and short-grass patches, compost store, water butt and bench.
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt; the Grounds line shows 607 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette. The walk check is ok and the overhead render reads as beds, paths and fence.
Plan.md's checklist (grounds) and elements 18–23 are ticked; bed geometry changed slightly from plan.md and is recorded in its Notes.
polish: Bed boxes differ from plan.md's ranges (bed 1 z31..35 not z30..35; bed 4 x3..9 not x2..9) so each spruce-slab ring fits the fence, water butt and other parts; recorded in plan.md Notes.
Lamp post lantern height and the fruit-tree crown were not inspected close up; only the overhead view was rendered.
The hanging orphans reported by mcd check (spruce slabs at x5/x18 z3/z24 y23, logs at 16,26,11 / 14,28,11 / 16,26,16) are in other parts' cells, not the garden.

waste.what: Worked out the gardenBed ring, fence corner and passage cell overlaps by hand (e.g. bed 1's ring hitting the water butt at 12,29, bed 2/3 rings meeting at z30, bed 4's ring hitting the west fence at x1), and fixed them by trial make.sh runs.

waste.what: Checked the garden by eye from the overhead render and read the placed cells one by one for the passage, gravel edges and tree ground patches.

waste.what: A sed edit to drop an unused import failed on macOS (BSD sed needs `-i ''`).
waste.cost: 1 retry
waste.tool: Use the Edit tool for in-file changes; no toolkit change needed.

Check the fruit tree's trunk height and crown spread against the fence, the bed ring at z33 and the west garden, and confirm the persistent oak leaves.
Build the gravel and coarse-dirt edges along the passage and path b so the mix reads as worn ground, not stripes.

summary:
room: Lobby stair hall: Lobby stair hall furnished in parts/room-1.mjs: coat post, lantern and boot bench by the front door, boot barrel with flower pot, and a table (fence + slab, candle) with chair south of the stair foot; the lane x5..6 stays clear.
Lit by 8 hanging lanterns (lane centre and west column, one over the table) plus standing lanterns on the coat post and the boot barrel; room check OK: walk 69 of 70 reachable, min light 7, 0 dark, 8 dim.
make.sh builds a whole build.nbt with 17 blocks for this part, no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE writes; room.png rendered and read (the view from above shows the stair, not the furniture at this scale).
polish: plan.md's checklist has no room-1 entry, so nothing was ticked; elements.md item 24 (lighting) is shared with the hearth part and was not ticked.
The one unreached cell (x7, z21) is the barrel top, which the standing lantern now occupies; it is not a floor cell anyone needs, but the room check still lists it as unreached.
8 floor cells remain at light 1-7 (the room check suggests a standing lantern at 5,6,11, which would block the lane, so it was not added).

waste.cost: 2 rebuilds
waste.tool: mcd room's unreached list could name the blocking block (lantern on barrel top) rather than only the cell coordinates.

companions.task: Light the 8 remaining dim floor cells (1-7) without putting a lamp in the lane: hidden light under the first-floor floor or a lantern tucked on the coat post side, so every cell is 8+.
Make the table and chair as real joinery (a fence table with a slab top, a stair chair) and check their facing against the stair foot, so the furniture reads as made rather than placed.

summary:
room: Keeper's aisle: Keeper's aisle (x10..13, z16..21, y6..12) is furnished in parts/room-2.mjs: barrel stores along the back wall, a stripped dark oak log butcher's block with a slab top as the focal piece, and hung lanterns from the y13 floor on a chain.
Walk is OK (24/24 cells reachable), the lane from the lobby door x9 z20 to the aisle doorway x14 z20..21 stays clear, and light is min 8 with 0 dark and 0 dim cells.
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt: this part placed 16 blocks with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE writes, and check reports 0 floating and 0 unsupported blocks (no orphans inside the room).
polish: plan.md's checklist has no room entries, so nothing was ticked; elements.md item 24 (lighting) names the hearth part, so I left it for that part and only note the aisle lanterns here.
The room.png view was too small to confirm the furniture by eye, so the layout is verified by the walk and light checks only; no zoomed interior view was rendered.
The aisle's cold-store feel is light (barrels, a butcher's block, chain-hung lanterns); no meat hooks or rail were added.

waste.what: Furniture drawn as layers per y level, with the legend and character grid worked out by hand against the plan's floor grid.
waste.cost: About 6 layer rows and 1 legend, one rewrite for the slab type (top vs bottom) and one for a missing standing lantern to light the lane.
waste.tool: A mcd plan variant that emits a blank layers() template per y with the free cells marked, so the furniture only needs filling in.

waste.what: Checking the light by hand: I guessed lantern spots and reran make.sh and the room check to see whether they cleared the dim lane cells.
waste.cost: Two make.sh runs (about 30 s each) and one room check per guess.
waste.tool: `$MCD room --suggest-apply` or a flag that writes the top suggested lantern spot into a copy so the check runs once.

waste.what: Reading room.png: the default from-above view is too small to show a 4x6 room's furniture, so I could only confirm the walls, not the layout.
waste.cost: One Read of the image, which was inconclusive about the furniture.
waste.tool: `$MCD rooms --only "<room>" --eye` or a zoomed per-room render with the furniture visible (the eye view from the door).

companions.task: Place the aisle's lanterns and check the light map once the lobby's stair hall is built, so the aisle's lantern spots do not double up with the lobby's light.
Pick the aisle's meat-hook and rail details (chain and hook shapes) and the barrel contents so the cold-store feel reads at the door, not just in the room check.

summary:
room: Wing kitchen and scullery: Wing kitchen and scullery furnished in parts/room-3.mjs: brick range with lit furnace and smoker on the south wall (x7..8 z29) in line with the lobby door, a worktable with two stair chairs, pantry barrels on the west wall, scullery sink and worktop under the kitchen window, and seven lanterns (six hanging from the y13 floor, one standing) for 0 dark cells.
The room check says OK: 42 of 42 floor cells reachable, light min 8, mean 10.5, no dark or dim cells. make.sh produced a whole build.nbt with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE writes for this part; door cells x6 z23 and x10 z27 are kept clear.
Rendered the room sheet (room.png); the from-above view reads, but the inside view does not show the range, so the focal piece is not yet confirmed from inside.
polish: Ownership conflict with hearth.mjs: the wing range at x7..8 z29 is listed in elements.md item 14 (hearth part), but this room part also builds it; whichever part runs first wins and the other's writes are refused. I added a Notes line in plan.md; the hearth worker should leave those cells to room-3 or the two should be reconciled.
The inside render does not clearly show the range at the south wall; the focal piece should be checked from the lobby door once the shell and hearth are merged.
room-3 is not a checklist item in plan.md and no elements.md item maps to it, so nothing was ticked.

waste.what: Mapped the plan grid's characters to world coordinates by hand (x = 4 + column index, z = 22 + row index) and wrote out each furniture row as a text string.
waste.cost: about 7 rows x 6 columns per layer, two layers, plus one correction pass after the first draft; no separate retries of blocks.
waste.tool: A `mcd plan --emit-legend` or `layers` variant that takes the plan grid itself with a per-character legend and returns the placed set, so the furnisher copies only the furniture characters rather than re-deriving origin offsets.

waste.tool: `mcd room --apply` or a lamp-placement mode that writes the suggested lantern spots into the part, so the lamplighter does not iterate by hand.

waste.cost: one read of elements.md and plan.md; the conflict only shows at merge time.
waste.tool: A `runParts` pre-check that lists which cells two parts both claim (a reserved-cell manifest per part) before the parallel build.

companions.task: Agree who builds the wing range at x7..8 z29 and its flue cells, so the furnace and smoker are placed once and the lit range reads as the room's focal piece from the lobby door.
Check the lantern spots against the final shell's ceiling so the six hanging lanterns hang from real y13 floor blocks, and confirm the standing pantry lantern at 5,6,27 once the floor is merged.

summary:
room: First-floor stair hall: First-floor stair hall furnished in parts/room-4.mjs: a spruce-stair settle facing east with a fence-and-slab table, a barrel store at the south-west corner, and four hanging lanterns (min light 8, no dark cells).
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE writes for this part; `mcd room` says OK.
The north strip x5..8 z7..12 (18 cells) is walk-unreachable from the arrival because the stair well and flight 2's steps cut it off. I left it bare and noted it in plan.md Notes.
polish: North strip x5..8 z7..12 (18 floor cells) is not walk-reachable from the stair arrival: the well at x7..8 z10..15 and flight 2's steps at x5..6 z12..15 cut it off, and the living-room door x9 z12 opens onto the well. The room is furnished only on the reachable cells; the stair joiner or the plan needs a landing or bridge at y14 over the well.
The room.png render was a small overhead view; I looked at it once and did not refine the furniture beyond the settle, table, barrels and lanterns.

waste.what: Worked out by hand which floor cells were walkable from the plan grid, where ' ' (well) and 'o' (stair and rail) were ambiguous; the north-strip cut-off only showed after the first make and room check.
waste.cost: one make.sh cycle plus a room check, and a re-read of flight 2 and the well coordinates from the spec
waste.tool: `mcd plan --rooms` could print reachability from the entrance (the same flood `mcd walk` uses) and a legend for ' ' (well or hole), so cut-off cells show before any furniture is drawn.

waste.what: Drew the furniture layers as text with layers() but laid out each y-level by hand, and placed the table top as a second layers() call for y15.
waste.cost: about 6 rows of hand-typed characters and one extra call; coordinate bookkeeping for the stair cells was done by reasoning
waste.tool: a `furnish` helper taking a per-y legend of furniture in room coordinates, that checks each cell against the plan grid and the walk before writing.

waste.what: Looked at the render with one view from above, which is too small to judge the furniture at this scale.
waste.cost: one render and one Read
waste.tool: `mcd rooms --tiles` or a zoom centred on the room's floor at a larger scale.

companions.task: Give the stairwell well and flight 2's foot a landing or a bridge at y14, so the north strip x5..8 z7..12 is reachable from the arrival and the living-room door at x9 z12 is no longer over the hole.
Check the light plan for the north strip once it is reachable, so the lanterns I hung there (x6 z9, x8 z13) are the right spots and the strip stays lit.

summary:
room: Living room: Living room furnished in parts/room-5.mjs: sofa on the north wall, two armchairs and a table facing the east hearth, bookshelves and a barrel on the west side, red carpet rug, one table pot and four hanging lanterns (one over the doorway lane).
./make.sh gives a whole build.nbt; this part places 24 blocks with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines. `mcd room` says OK: 81/81 floor cells reachable, min light 8, no dark cells.
The hearth on the east wall is not in this copy's build (its part is a stub here), so the inside render shows no focal fireplace yet; the doorway lane (x10..17 z12, x17 z13..14) is kept clear for it.
polish: Stair facing convention unverified: I used the toolkit's rule (facing = side of the full-height back) for the sofa and armchairs, so their seats face south and east. A render from the hearth's side should confirm they face the room.
Hearth (x18 z13..14, y14..16) is built by parts/hearth.mjs, which is a stub in this copy, so the focal fireplace does not appear in the render here; the room's lane is kept clear for it.
No plan.md checklist item or elements.md row maps to the living room, so none was ticked.

waste.what: Worked out the furniture cell by cell from the plan grid, then re-derived the grid's column offsets (x8 is the stair hall, x9 the partition with the doorway, x10..18 the floor) because the plan's 'o' marks the partition wall as furniture.
waste.cost: about 4 coordinate passes and one wrong reading of the x origin before the layout was right
waste.tool: `mcd plan` should print the floor's real x range and label wall-line cells as 'wall' rather than 'o', so the origin is unambiguous
